sections.value:
Security verdict, #306 (F249) at be097a697256ffad0ad1a933706f0650342180f1: PASS WITH NOTES. Static review of the change (6d48297d), the manifest (589847e0) and the merges; CI 5/5 green and CLEAN at this head (gh pr view 306). I ran no build and no live canary.

Trust model (C33). The canary checks for accidental misattribution. It does not prove anything against an adversarial seat. Both of its sources are same-user, harness-written self-reports. The native record is the seat's own transcript under ~/.omp/agent/sessions, so the seat can append to it with a bash tool. The footer is the seat's own pane. C33 trusts the user account, so neither source was ever proof against a same-user seat, and this PR doesn't change that. The canary's purpose survives, and the native source is stronger for the honest case: OMP 18.16 writes model_change to the file at once (session-manager.ts appendModelChange -> #recordEntry -> #appendToSessionFile, lazily only before the first assistant message). It also records the model that actually answered on each assistant entry, fallbacks included. When the challenge ack is a model turn, the record names the model that answered it.

Checked and clean:
- Freshness: the pane and native_session_id check now runs before the model is chosen. Native is read only for seat.harness_session, which is the same id that check just compared, and an empty id gives None. UnisphereSessionStatus keeps no cache of good reads (only a NotFound miss TTL, which falls back to the footer), so a canary reads the current tail incrementally.
- native_model_of trusts only a native, non-empty Fact::Known with no pending switch. Unknown, derived, NotFound, Unsupported and Err all fall back to the footer, and no source refuses.
- omp models launch: the site (models.rs run_omp_command) already existed and records omp.models. It runs through pij_core::program::launch, which resolves PATH to an absolute path. argv is fixed: models --json --no-extensions. No footer text reaches argv or env. It inherits the daemon env, writes stdout and stderr to temp files and has a timeout. spawn_sites.rs scans crates/harnesses, so the site stays covered.
- Footer parse: fails closed, and its scope is narrower than the old "last line containing U+2B22". It needs the last line with U+25EB and exactly one icon+space+non-level-word segment; two segments, a glued glyph or no-model give None. My 2026-11-19 note still applies (a quoted footer is not provenance): a model's output is read only if it is the last U+25EB line. It is a fallback now.
- Catalog: stripping "Claude " only adds a match. The existing duplicate-match check still refuses an ambiguous name, and a partial name still refuses.
- Fixtures (C21): 130 and 110 bytes, sha256 matches MANIFEST, no ESC bytes, no home paths, no secrets. They contain seat names, an extension hash and a session cost figure, all public-safe.

Notes (non-blocking):
- S306-N1 (fail-open edge): unisphere returns pending_switch: None when it can't order the switch against the last call (pending_known=false: a timestamp missing on one side). pij maps that to modelSwitchPending=false and trusts the old model. A switch and a call in the same millisecond (at > call) also count as not pending. OMP 18.16 always stamps both, so this is unreachable for OMP today. But native_runtime_model applies to every harness, so I'd treat "model.pending_switch" in the status's unknown list as pending.
- S306-N2 (hardening): when both sources answer, native wins and the footer is not consulted. The footer is already observed and resolved, so refusing when the two disagree would cost nothing. It would also catch an atomic-batch delay in writing the switch and any record or render drift. Optional.
